caption: Each input pulse makes exactly one lit TNT and throws it away: it lands 14 to 18 blocks from the machine and explodes there, and a TNT blast cannot break anything more than about 7 blocks away, so the machine is safe standing right on the ground. Detail: the switchable 12-block engine with a slime launcher (each TNT flung at 1 block per tick) and an active-low input (at rest a redstone block in the input spot holds the piston out; the pulse takes it away for one push); one obsidian foot under the piston keeps the moving slimes off the grass (a slime frame resting on grass drags it). Measured on redsim at every kick angle: on grass the explosions are 14.2 to 18.5 blocks away, on obsidian 14.2; 0 machine blocks destroyed

The fast TNT duplicator: 200 lit TNT a minute, each thrown away at 1 block per tick, but it must stand at least 8 blocks above the ground: lower down, the TNT pile up 10 to 20 blocks away and every blast throws some of them back within the ~7 blocks a blast can break. At 8 blocks up they explode 12 to 59 blocks away and it survives (0 blocks destroyed, also over a 10-minute run). Detail: the 12-block core with its stone turned into a slime chain that carries a slime over the TNT cell and flings every TNT north; for world eaters and cannons fed from a tower. Measured on redsim at every kick angle at an 8-block drop: grass 11.8 to 54.3 blocks away, obsidian 11.7 to 59.1

A self-running TNT duplicator that is safe standing right on the ground: a small clock lets it make one TNT every 91 ticks and throw it away; each lands 14 to 18 blocks from the machine and explodes before the next one is made, so no blast ever throws a TNT back, and a blast breaks nothing beyond about 7 blocks. Detail: the 12-block engine with its slime launcher, held by a 7-block crafter-loop clock that releases it for one push per period (the hold extended by a 4-tick repeater loop so the release is a single push); 13.2 TNT per minute. Measured on redsim at every kick angle: on grass the explosions are 14.2 to 18.5 blocks away, on obsidian 14.2; 0 machine blocks destroyed

Every lit TNT is thrown against a stone wall that stops it dead and then falls straight down, so this duplicator only works over a deep pit: it needs at least 31 blocks of air under it; then the TNT explode 24 to 36 blocks below and around it, too far for a blast (which breaks nothing beyond about 7 blocks) to reach it. On the ground it blows itself up within seconds. Detail: the launching duper plus one stone as a north wall. Measured on redsim at every kick angle, at a 31-block drop: grass 23.6 to 35.7 blocks away, obsidian 30.9 to 32.9; 0 machine blocks destroyed

Every lit TNT explodes at exactly the same point in the air, 9 blocks up, bit for bit: a slow duplicator throws each TNT into a little water channel where the current pins it against a wall (that cancels the random sideways kick every TNT gets when it is lit), and 55 ticks after it was lit a slime piston under it launches it straight up, so it is flying at its highest point when its fuse runs out. Detail: the precise duper engine (a 91-tick crafter-loop clock, one TNT at a time) flings each TNT 9 blocks north into the aligner channel; an observer next to the engine sees each push and a line of repeaters (55 ticks of delay) fires the upward piston; measured on redsim at every kick angle, on grass and obsidian ground: every explosion at (3.51, 8.45, -9.51) from the design origin, 0 blocks destroyed; safe on the ground

The fast TNT duplicator with an on/off switch: a redstone torch placed next to its piston holds it still; take the torch away and it throws a lit TNT every 6 ticks. Like the fast one it must stand a few blocks above the ground (lower down, the pile of landed TNT gets thrown back at it). Detail: the 12-block core held by power on its sticky piston, plus the slime-chain launcher; the input is a torch on a stone (the judge places and removes it), because a repeater line driving the input stops it restarting
